Key Activities: Directs complex assignments involving in-depth and unique studies in an area of specialization impacting a number of subject matter areas; develops the overall conclusions and recommendations; reviews and approves analytical material and research papers for publication.
Provides authoritative analysis and advice to senior officials at all levels of government, industry, academia, other national and international institutions and special interest groups.
Reviews proposals to develop new methods and techniques to meet the needs of unique studies and assesses the implications of new approaches.
Determines the extent of major studies and establishes the overall parameters and objectives and determines the need for additional reviews.
Directs the work of multi-disciplinary departmental and interdepartmental project teams, working groups and committees involved in research and analytical activities.
Represents the federal government and broad Canadian interests while presenting options and strategies to develop research studies on complex policy issues of interest to a variety of stakeholders.

1. Decision making: Directs the conduct of in-depth and unique studies in an area of specialization or wide-ranging and extensive reviews extending across a number of subject matter areas and determines the broad objectives and content of studies and develops solutions to complex methodology issues.

Directs the conduct of research studies on policy issues impacting on major departmental entities across government, determines the extent of such studies, establishes the overall parameters and objectives, provides expert analysis and interpretation of results, develops the overall conclusions and presents advice and recommendations to senior executives.

As a departmental expert, provides authoritative recommendations and expert advice to senior officials and policy advisors within and outside Statistics Canada on the results of unique economic and socio-economic studies and their impact on major program, policy or regulatory issues.

Recommends new research priorities and initiatives to senior management; reviews strategic directions for the management of significant research studies, recommends innovative solutions to address departmental goals and objectives and approves analytical material and research papers for publication.
2. Leadership and operational management: Directs the work of multi-disciplinary, departmental and interdepartmental project teams, working groups and committees involved in significant research and analytical activities.

Develops plans and objectives and allocates human and financial resources to ensure that these goals are met. Directs recruitment activities, identifies experience and knowledge requirements and selects project staff. Prepares performance appraisals for subordinate staff and resolves performance and disciplinary matters.
Negotiates and approves contracts with consulting firms. Selects contractors for specific projects. Assigns, directs, manages and evaluates the work according to contract specifications.
3. Communication: As a departmental expert, provides advice and recommendations to senior officials within and outside Statistics Canada on the results of unique economic and socio-economic studies and their impact on major program or regulatory issues.

Defends proposals for the development of new research initiatives to address current socio-economic trends and developments at the national and international levels, and negotiates the allocation of funding for the conduct of such studies and projects.

Represents the department in discussions where consensus must be achieved on major issues which impact the programs and/or policies of other government departments, industries and special interest groups. At this level, there is a particular requirement to deal with sensitive and political issues that could embarrass the department.

Writing skills to prepare and review research papers, articles and reports and to determine and assess the design and content of studies, articles and reports that will be disseminated widely or published.
Chairs intra-departmental meetings and participates in inter-departmental meetings, conferences and groups to develop consensus or share knowledge in a particular field.
Represents the federal government and broad Canadian interests while presenting options and strategies to develop research studies on complex policy issues of interest to a variety of stakeholders.
4. Knowledge of specialized fields: Expert knowledge of advanced economic or sociologic theories and principles relating to a specialized subject area to provide authoritative and expert advice to senior officials and policy advisors within and outside Statistics Canada on the results of unique economic and socio-economic studies and their impact on major program, policy or regulatory issues.

A deep understanding of the underlying theoretical concepts of economics, sociology and statistics as they relate to a group of specialized areas to develop and implement programs to produce statistics covering a wide range of issues.

Knowledge of writing and editing skills and techniques to write and review research papers, articles and reports and to determine and assess the design and content of studies, articles and reports that will be disseminated widely or published.

Knowledge of the principles and practices of management with regards to human and financial resources in order to direct the work multi-disciplinary departmental and interdepartmental project teams, working groups and committees.
5. Contextual knowledge: Knowledge of current and emerging socio-economic and political issues in Canada in relation to that of other industrialized countries such as the changed social context and the globalization of markets, as they relate to all the aspects of a variety of statistical programs. This knowledge is necessary to defend proposals for the development of new research initiatives.

Knowledge of governmental policies, programs and regulatory issues in order to provide expert advice to senior officials and policy advisors, within and outside Statistics Canada, on the results and impact of unique economic and socio-economic studies.
Knowledge of the Department’s strategic direction, goals and objectives, is required in order to contribute to their development.

Knowledge of the division mandate and priorities as well as subject-matter expertise in order to review strategic directions in the management of significant research studies, and to recommend innovative solutions to address departmental goals and objectives.

Knowledge of the policies and programs of key client departments in order to mediate with their representatives to reach a consensus on the major issues affecting departments, industries and special interest groups, and to recommend priorities for new research initiatives.

Knowledge of the Statistics Act and other pertinent acts such as the Corporate Returns Act and Income Tax Act, and of Statistics Canada policies to explain legislative and policy requirements to other departments, agencies, industry, members of the public and the media. Knowledge of the Statitstics and Privacy Acts is particulary important with respect to the security and confidentiality of information and data provided and to ensure that they and their subordinates do not release any information which may identify an individual or group without prior consent.
Knowledge of a variety of Acts related to the area of expertise such as the Income Tax Act, the Excise Sales Tax Act, the Employment Insurance Act, and the Corporate Returns Act.
6. Research and analysis: Directs the conduct of high-profile research studies on policy issues impacting on major departmental entities across government, determines the extent of such studies, establishes the overall parameters and objectives, provides expert analysis and interpretation of results, and presents authoritative recommendations to senior executives.

Analyses current socio-economic trends and developments at the national and international levels, determines the implications of proposed areas of study, defends proposals for the development of new research initiatives and negotiates the allocation of funding for the conduct of studies and projects.

Reviews strategic directions for the management of significant research studies, recommends innovative solutions to address departmental goals and objectives and approves analytical material and research papers for publication.
Develops new methods, concepts and definitions to meet the needs of the most unique studies, assesses the implications of new approaches and develops solutions to complex methodology issues.

Analyses the impact of study results on major program, policy and regulatory issues and provides authoritative and expert advice to senior officials and policy advisors within and outside of Statistics Canada.
